title: I Let the Bagpipe-Chanter Hours Catch the Pipe Major Who Camped My Numbered Reed

parts.text: I stepped into the pipe hall at 6:05 p.m. and pipe major Dougal was already using numbered gear. The board said: ONE CHANTER. FORTY MINUTES. REEDS STAY WITH THE SLOT. I was thirty-four, band secretary, holding a clipboard that listed our numbered reeds. Dougal shrugged. "Majors are the drones." I photographed the board, the booking, and his leftover hemp on my numbered reed. Then I asked for the chanter log. At 6:13 the hall pinged why Dougal's name was on my hemp. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The hall can see Dougal's leftover hemp on my numbered reed.

social.video_title: He camped my numbered chanter reed on my slot — Part 1/2
social.description: Pipe hall, leftover hemp, a forty-minute clock he posted. I logged the chanter. Would you have asked for the chanter log?

parts.text: Dougal called it reed seating until the hall asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the hemp still. The reed went back to my numbered slot. Dougal ran a slot of his own and told the next major atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: MAJORS ARE NOT THE DRONES. I keep my reeds in a labeled case. Dougal brown-bags his seating. The hall finally looks like a slot, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Majors are not the drones — Part 2/2
social.description: Chanter log, numbered reed, and a second line on the board. Was reed seating ever my hemp?
